provenance.canonical_layout: SEC XBRL company-concept payloads captured verbatim from data.sec.gov for the balance-sheet concepts, plus the canonical daily price series and filing acceptance index reused by path from data/historical_pe/MSFT, and the cover-page shares outstanding series reused by path from data/historical_pfcf/MSFT. The trailing revenue and EBITDA denominators are the data/historical_income/MSFT dataset's own windows, executed from its config, never recomputed here.

concept_fetch.transport: HTTPS GET data.sec.gov/api/xbrl/companyconcept/CIK0000789019/us-gaap/{tag}.json with a declared contactable User-Agent, honouring the SEC fair-access policy
concept_fetch.response_units: verbatim as returned: USD for all five concepts

cash_concept.json.definition: Cash and cash equivalents at carrying value, the liquid-funds component of the filed EV bridge.

marketable_securities_current_concept.js.definition: Microsoft's current marketable securities. It reports the line as 'Short-term investments' and carries it on us-gaap:ShortTermInvestments; it does not use us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesCurrent at all, so the bridge's role is filled by the element the issuer uses. First carried from FY2018 filings.

commercial_paper_concept.json.definition: Commercial paper, a total-debt component of the filed EV bridge alongside the two long-term debt concepts. Microsoft stopped tagging the line after the FY2025 10-K, which is why the last evaluation dates carry a stale component and publish no enterprise value.

long_term_debt_current_concept.json.definition: Current portion of long-term debt, a total-debt component of the filed EV bridge.

long_term_debt_noncurrent_concept.json.definition: Long-term debt, non-current, a total-debt component of the filed EV bridge.

daily_prices.json (reused by path).source: The canonical production historical P/E dataset's price series, read by path. Microsoft has had no stock split since 2003, so the series needs no split adjustment and the as-traded close pairs with the cover-page share count as it stands.

filing_acceptance_evidence.json (reused.source: The canonical historical P/E dataset's acceptance index: each filing's acceptance datetime, form and period end. A fact whose filing is not in the index has no knowability evidence in this dataset and is skipped.

shares_outstanding_concept.json (reused.source: The canonical cover-page shares outstanding series from the historical P/FCF dataset, read by path so one share series serves every market-cap reconstruction. Counts are never split-adjusted and pair with the as-traded close.

provenance.point_in_time_rule: usable_date is derived from acceptance_datetime_header_et using the 16:00 ET cutoff rule at load time, identical to the historical P/E, P/FCF and income pipelines. The value in force at an evaluation date is the latest knowable version of each component; no fact is used before its filing's usable date.

multiple_rules.ps: P/S = (as-traded close on the evaluation date x latest knowable cover-page shares outstanding) / TTM revenue, where the TTM revenue window is the income dataset's own four-consecutive-fiscal-quarter window. A non-positive denominator produces no multiple.
multiple_rules.ev_ebitda: EV/EBITDA = (market capitalization + total debt [long-term debt non-current + long-term debt current + commercial paper] - liquid funds [cash and cash equivalents + current marketable securities]) / TTM EBITDA. Every bridge component must be knowable at the evaluation date, and every one of them must describe the SAME balance-sheet date: a date whose components span more than one balance sheet publishes no enterprise value, with the reason REASON_MIXED_BALANCE_SHEET_PERIODS. The bridge is never completed by omission, substitution or zero-fill, and a component that was not reported is not carried forward as zero. Market capitalization is not a balance-sheet component and is not part of the same-date rule. The bridge remains a partial statement of enterprise value even when complete (it omits leases, non-current investments and off-balance sheet claims) and every observation says so. For Microsoft the denominator does not exist at all: the income-statement dataset holds no element that qualifies for the depreciation-and-amortization role, so no trailing EBITDA window exists and every date refuses with REASON_NO_QUALIFIED_DA_EVIDENCE.

provenance.reference_gate: The same >= 20 qualifying observations rule as every other production distribution. A thinner sample stays descriptive and is never a scenario exit multiple. The two distributions are qualified independently: one qualifying does not qualify the other.
known_limitations: The trailing EBITDA denominator does not exist for Microsoft: the income-statement dataset holds no element that qualifies for the depreciation-and-amortization role, so no trailing EBITDA window is constructed and the EV/EBITDA distribution has no qualifying observation. The P/S distribution qualifies on 23 observations.

The EV bridge would not have qualified the distribution either: only 8 of the 27 evaluation dates have all five components describing one balance sheet, because Microsoft disclosed its commercial paper through the fair-value note until the FY2025 10-K -- an explicit zero at 2025-06- 30 and 6,693 million at 2024-06-30 -- and has not reported it at all since. The 15 earlier evaluation dates have no commercial-paper evidence inside the acceptance index, and the last four carry the stale 2025-06-30 fact, which the same-date rule refuses.
The reconstructed enterprise value omits operating leases, non-current investments and off-balance sheet commitments. It is labelled partial on every observation.
The evaluation dates are the filing usable dates shared with the income reconstruction, not a continuous daily trading history.

semantic_qualification.policy: A source element is qualified for a metric only when the core registry resolves it to that metric for that filer: an EXACT IDENTITY mapping, in force at the date read, whose scope covers the filer. An element the registry declines, retires, maps only partially, maps to another metric or scopes to another filer is not qualified, and its filed values produce no figure and no production reference. Holding a filed element as traceable evidence is not the same as admitting it to a valuation.
semantic_qualification.read_by: the core registry, as seeded from registry_seed
semantic_qualification.subject: MSFT multiples dataset

revenue.basis: The core registry maps us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax to 'revenue' for MSFT as an EXACT IDENTITY mapping, without a filer restriction, in force from 2017-09-30. The element is this metric for this filer, and its filed values may produce a figure.

operating_income.basis: The core registry maps us-gaap:OperatingIncomeLoss to 'operating_income' for MSFT as an EXACT IDENTITY mapping, without a filer restriction. The element is this metric for this filer, and its filed values may produce a figure.

depreciation_and_amortization.basis: No element fills the depreciation-and-amortization role for MSFT. The role is empty, so the metric has no source for this filer and no trailing EBITDA window can exist at any date.

cash.basis: The core registry maps us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsAtCarryingValue to 'cash' for MSFT as an EXACT IDENTITY mapping, without a filer restriction. The element is this metric for this filer, and its filed values may produce a figure.

marketable_securities_current.basis: The registry declares no marketable_securities_current metric, so it cannot rule on the element this component is read from. The filed-bridge specification governs this component, and the element is read under it.

commercial_paper.basis: The registry declares no commercial_paper metric, so it cannot rule on the element this component is read from. The filed-bridge specification governs this component, and the element is read under it.

long_term_debt_noncurrent.basis: The core registry maps us-gaap:LongTermDebtNoncurrent to 'long_term_debt_noncurrent' for MSFT as an EXACT IDENTITY mapping, without a filer restriction, in force from 2014-09-27. The element is this metric for this filer, and its filed values may produce a figure.

long_term_debt_current.basis: The core registry maps us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent to 'long_term_debt_current' for MSFT as an EXACT IDENTITY mapping, without a filer restriction, in force from 2014-09-27. The element is this metric for this filer, and its filed values may produce a figure.
